items.title: Charles Calello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 21, 2025
items.q: And one of the guitar players said to the other guitar player, who was like Lou, doing sessions, he said, “See I told you, Calello used to write the parts out.”

ctx.x: Here’s what – see because I never did anybody else, I never went to anybody else’s sessions. So as an arranger I had no idea what other guys did. I only knew what they did on the records. So in order to control the speed of how we can get the feel, I started to write the guitar parts out. I would write the rhythms and I would write some of the licks. And I would indicate where I wanted the licks. And then I would write simile. But

basically when I used three guitars or four guitars, I wrote the parts out. Not the little – like I would write the rhythms and I’d indicate when they should play where. And I didn’t realize I did that until I went to California and I came back to New York after about a year and a half later and I did an orchestra date. And one of the guitar players said to the other guitar player, who was like Lou, doing sessions, he said, “See I told you, Calello used to write the parts out.” So, and I heard him say that and…
You didn’t know you were doing something that most other people didn’t.
